channel.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
channel.description: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

item.title: New York's laws on consent and alcohol use could complicate Cornell case prosecution
item.description: NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with Erin Murphy, a professor at NYU School of Law and an expert on sexual assault law, about how New York state considers alcohol use when determining the presence of consent.
item.content:encoded: NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with Erin Murphy, a professor at NYU School of Law and an expert on sexual assault law, about how New York state considers alcohol use when determining the presence of consent.

item.title: 'The Third Eye' presents an unfiltered view of the Beatles' early years
item.description: NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with Olivia Harrison about the new book The Third Eye, a collection of photographs by her late husband, George Harrison of the Beatles.
item.content:encoded: NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with Olivia Harrison about the new book The Third Eye, a collection of photographs by her late husband, George Harrison of the Beatles.

item.title: NPR spoke to Cuban men now stuck in limbo in Central African Republic
item.description: Thousands of people have been sent to countries they have no ties to and in some cases have never even heard of as part of the Trump administration's drive toward mass deportations.

item.title: With a voice as vast as the ocean, Beth Taylor has arrived
item.description: The up-and-coming Scottish mezzo-soprano's debut recital album is a compelling collection of songs about the sea.

item.title: There's a contraception shortage in Tanzania due to a cut in U.S. family planning aid
item.description: The U.S. supplied the majority of Tanzania's birth control until it was abruptly cut off in 2025. It's unclear how the country will fill the gaps.
item.content:encoded: The U.S. supplied the majority of Tanzania's birth control until it was abruptly cut off in 2025. It's unclear how the country will fill the gaps.

item.title: Supreme Court term is now underway. Here's what we're watching
item.description: Monday kicked off the new Supreme Court term, one that will once again be full of controversial topics from religion to guns and immigration.

item.title: DJ_Dave's 'Hardcore Software' is code you can dance to
item.description: DJ_Dave writes and performs dance music with code. Her debut album, Hardcore Software, combines tech optimism with the open source spirit of an algorave.

item.title: Drones buzz overhead, troops hunker underground in Ukraine's hellish kill zone
item.description: The front line in the Russia-Ukraine war stretches more than 700 miles and has barely moved in four years. Yet straddling this line is the kill zone, dominated by constantly evolving drone technology.

item.title: Cineplexity: Can Hollywood make video game movies that stand on their own?
item.description: Hollywood wants to tap into the built-in audience for video games. NPR's Stephen Thompson and Vincent Acovino discuss what it takes to make a video game adaptation that works beyond its fan base.

item.description: Brazil's environment is a global concern. But on the campaign trail, it's struggling to get voters' attention.
